newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE wheat, barley futures up, maize mixed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE wheat, barley futures up, maize mixed.

text.p: Wheat and barley prices went up while maize ended mixed in the grain section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Tuesday, this year's first day with a sizeable turnover.
"This was a modest average turnover," said Robert Vajo of Termin Broker.
One reason for the continuing rise of old (1996) crop milling wheat prices is market talk about Serbian and Bosnian buying intentions.
"This supports prices, although the (sales) volumes will probably be relatively small," Vajo said.
New (1997) crop milling wheat prices continued their rise on unfounded fears that cold weather could endanger the crop.
"These rises have more to do with market psychology than with specialists' assessments," Vajo said.
Milling wheat prices closed at 29,320 forints for March and 24,500 forints for the December delivery.
Vajo said he expects wheat prices to remain volatile until at least the end of March. Feed barley prices rose the limit for all deliveries, for two reasons.
"On the one hand there is no surplus of the old crop, on the other, new crop prices went up in response to rising wheat prices," Vajo said.
Maize prices ended mixed with the March delivery closing at 20,000 forints, up 200 and July also at 20,000 but down 300.
"The fact that export licenses were extended until the end of March supports prices but I expect a slight downward trend to start in the second quarter of this year," Vajo said.
Total turnover was 647.2 million forints or 1,464 contracts, of which 695 were maize and 742 milling wheat and the remaining 27 feed wheat.
(Lot size 20,000 kgs for all contracts. $=162.23 Hungarian forints) --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
